paper_operator: Section 2.1 explicitly permits the L2-orthogonal P_T operator in addition to vertex interpolation I_T; conforming triangulations/continuous piecewise functions are not required by that paper framework.
coverage: All fourteen previously fixed quartic field/rotation cases and all nine budgets, 126 pairs. No new favourable field/angle selection.
pilot_disclosure: An exploratory projection pilot already observed all fourteen cases at N=2048 and corrected a zero-area clipped-fan bug before this full protocol. This is a prospective fixed all-budget study following a disclosed pilot, not preregistration before all observations.
p1_projection: Project onto P1 locally on each exact previously saved interpolation-greedy triangle. Exact 3x3 barycentric mass inverse and seven-node degree-sufficient Gauss-Duffy load integration. This is a stronger approximation-operator control on the frozen mesh, not a newly PT-driven adaptive greedy mesh or author software.
ruled_projection: For the exact previously chosen mean-Hessian quadratic-ruled model per case/budget, change only Bezier Z coefficients by a shared-control global L2 projection. Keep every XY, index, patch, clip, C0 shared boundary and complete GPR3 byte count. Seven-node clipped-domain Galerkin assembly, matrix-free Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate gradient, 4096 iteration cap, relative residual tolerance 1e-12; recomputed true residual must be <=1e-11. No projection-space re-search.
metrics: Whole-domain E2 of actual saved Float64 models, independently integrated with five and seven Gauss-Duffy nodes over the same 10000 m2 square; retain original P1, original ruled and hierarchy-P2 controls. Record complete native binary costs including duplicated XYZ caused by discontinuous plane heights, not optimal plane-coefficient coding.
failures: Keep every fixed pair, including failed fitting/convergence, all losses and ties. No dropping failed or unfavourable pairs, no favourable tolerance or budget retuning after this protocol.
reporting: Finite shared-space fitting improvement and paper-permitted PT control on a frozen mesh. Not a refutation of the paper's asymptotic P1 theorem, a best-mesh proof, real-DTM accuracy, a continuous maximum-error certificate, runtime/RAM/GPU/ArcGIS benchmark or a universal high-order advantage. The existing hierarchy-P2 control remains explicit.
